anti_corruption_features: 16-bit LCRC at the Data Link Layer protects each TLP across the Link.
16-bit CRC at the Data Link Layer protects each DLLP.
32-bit ECRC (optional) at the Transaction Layer provides end-to-end TLP integrity.
128b/130b block sync-header + scrambler-lock checking catches block-framing errors at 32 GT/s before the DLL sees them.
ACK/NAK + Retry Buffer guarantees in-order delivery despite transient bit errors.
Sequence Number monotonicity detection rejects duplicate / out-of-order packets.
Lane Margining at the Receiver provides in-system signal-integrity diagnostics (margin health), reducing silent data-corruption risk at 32 GT/s.
future_security_pointers: PCI Express Integrity & Data Encryption (IDE) — AES-GCM link encryption + integrity; a separate ECN layered on PCIe 5.0+.
Component Measurement and Authentication (CMA) / SPDM — device attestation, layered above the base protocol.
Compute Express Link (CXL), running on the PCIe 5.0 PHY via Alternate Protocol Negotiation, adds CXL.io/CXL.cache/CXL.mem with its own CXL IDE link security.
Access Control Services (ACS) and SR-IOV — peer-to-peer routing restriction / VM isolation; NOT cryptographic.
fields.notes: PCI Express 5.0 base transactions are in plaintext on the Link; CRC + ECRC provide anti-corruption only. Cryptographic security (IDE link encryption, CMA/SPDM attestation) is provided by separate ECNs layered above the base PCIe 5.0 data path. The mandatory Lane Margining feature is a signal-integrity diagnostic, not a security feature.
